# SameSiteNoneWithoutSecure

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="tip" text="native" /> <Badge type="tip" text="on by default" /> <Badge type="info" text="PHP ≥ 7.3" />

Group: [Probable bugs](/rules/#probable-bugs)

Detect setcookie with literal options selecting SameSite None and secure absent or false.

## Example

```php{2}
<?php
setcookie('sid', 'abc', ['samesite' => 'None', 'secure' => false]);
```

Reported:

<ul>
<li>line 2: Use a Secure cookie with SameSite None.</li>
</ul>

## Detection

- Report setcookie with literal options selecting SameSite None and secure absent or false.
- Option names are compared without regard to letter case, as PHP does: `SameSite`, `SAMESITE`, `Secure` and `SECURE` name the same options as their lower-case spellings.
- Resolve builtin calls and named arguments before checking the contract. Project-local callees are considered only when their bodies or immutable summaries establish the required facts. The default is enabled, with positive proof required.
- For flow-dependent conditions, require a reachable source-to-use path with no intervening invalidation. Unknown calls, ambiguous aliases, recursion or analysis-budget exhaustion cannot establish definite facts.

## Exceptions (no report)

- Secure true, other SameSite policies, unknown options and unrelated user functions are excluded.
- An options array that spells one option name twice with different letter case is not reported: the effective value depends on entry order.
- Unresolved targets, incomplete required facts, suppressed findings and PHP versions lacking the referenced API or language feature produce no report. User declarations shadowing builtin names are not builtin contracts.

## Fix

No automatic fix: enabling Secure can make a cookie unusable on non-HTTPS deployments; document the HTTPS prerequisite.

## PHP versions

Available from PHP 7.3. Builtin behavior and argument contracts follow the configured PHP version. Extension-specific calls require resolved extension API symbols; do not treat same-named application functions as extension calls.

## Options

None. Enable or disable this rule through normal rule configuration.

## Configure

In [`custos.json`](/guide/configuration):

```json
{
  "rules": {
    "SameSiteNoneWithoutSecure": {
      "enabled": false
    }
  }
}
```

## Suppress

Before the statement or declaration (or the first statement of the file):

```php
// @custos-ignore SameSiteNoneWithoutSecure
```
